title: "Output & recessions"

```{ojs}
gdpc1 = await (await fetch("../data/fred/GDPC1.json")).json()
usrec = await (await fetch("../data/fred/USREC.json")).json()
```

```{ojs}
viewof gdp_window = Inputs.range([5, 75], {value: 35, step: 1, label: "Years to display"})
```

```{ojs}
// Compute QoQ growth rate (annualized) from real GDP
function qoq_annualized(obs) {
  const out = []
  for (let i = 1; i < obs.length; i++) {
    if (obs[i].value && obs[i-1].value) {
      const g = ((obs[i].value / obs[i-1].value) ** 4 - 1) * 100
      out.push({date: obs[i].date, value: g})
    }
  }
  return out
}
gdp_growth = qoq_annualized(gdpc1.observations)
```

```{ojs}
{
  const cutoff = new Date()
  cutoff.setFullYear(cutoff.getFullYear() - gdp_window)
  const filt = arr => arr.filter(d => new Date(d.date) >= cutoff).map(d => ({...d, date: new Date(d.date)}))
  const recs = filt(usrec.observations).filter(d => d.value === 1)
  return Plot.plot({
    width: 800, height: 380, marginLeft: 70, marginBottom: 50,
    x: {type: "utc"},
    y: {label: "Real GDP, billions of chained 2017 $ (log scale)", grid: true, type: "log"},
    marks: [
      // Recession bars
      Plot.rect(recs, {x1: "date", x2: (d, i) => i < recs.length-1 ? recs[i+1].date : new Date(), y1: 1, y2: 1e6, fill: "#cccccc", fillOpacity: 0.4}),
      Plot.line(filt(gdpc1.observations), {x: "date", y: "value", stroke: "#0e7c7b", strokeWidth: 2})
    ]
  })
}
```

```{ojs}
      <div class="kpi-sub">${units}</div>
    </div>
  `).join('')}
</div>`
```

## What to watch

A **recession** is officially declared by the [NBER Business Cycle Dating Committee](https://www.nber.org/research/business-cycle-dating). The shorthand is "two consecutive quarters of negative GDP growth," but the NBER actually weighs employment, real income, retail sales, and industrial production alongside GDP. The NBER lags real time — a recession usually starts months before it's officially declared and can be revised after the fact.

Real GDP growth above 2.5% is generally considered hot. Below 1% suggests slowdown. Negative for two quarters is the rule-of-thumb recession trigger.

## Source

[FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/) — GDPC1 (real GDP, chained 2017 dollars) from the BEA, quarterly. USREC (recession indicator) from NBER, monthly. Recession bars on the chart are the NBER-dated periods.
